Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modeled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
The Maxed rung — 3 color-legal Game Changers, about $94
Game Changer$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Crop Rotation$4Takes the ramp slot held by Sifter of Skulls. Search your library for a land card, put that card onto the battlefield, then shuffle.
Demonic Tutor$62Takes the tutor slot held by Fauna Shaman. Search your library for a card, put that card into your hand, then shuffle.
Worldly Tutor$28Takes the tutor slot held by Rune-Scarred Demon. Search your library for a creature card, reveal it, then shuffle and put the card on top.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are not a shortlist — they are the cards the Maxed hundred runs. Each was tried in several slots in the list it would join, kept only where the deck did not measurably get worse over 3,000 simulated games, and confirmed afterwards on a seed the selection never saw. Prices are Scryfall market values.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Still a graveyard deck, so it shares Muldrotha's exposure to Rest in Peace — take one of the two, not both. The Capstone budget is now fully deployed here: Elesh Norn and Craterhoof are the premium mutate payoffs, Broodmoth and Vigor make wipes a bad trade for everyone else.
Claude’s Runner-up

Second, now with the budget deployed: Elesh Norn and Craterhoof are premium mutate payoffs, Broodmoth and Vigor make every wipe a bad trade for everyone else, and Buried Alive makes the mutate surgical. Still a graveyard deck sharing the flagship's hate exposure — that is the whole gap to first.

Precon seed

Any Simic ramp shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$35 $141 total
Why this commander

Removes the two rules that cap a green deck: mana empties at end of turn, and hand size is seven. Unspent ramp becomes a stockpile instead of waste.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Nyxbloom Ancient{4}{G}{G}{G}Enchantment Creature — ElementalTriples all your mana. The convergence trigger.$26.34
Aesi, Tyrant of Gyre Strait{4}{G}{U}Legendary Creature — SerpentExtra land drops and a card each — in the 99 here.$11.10
Wall of Blossoms{1}{G}Creature — Plant WallCheap defense while you bank.$0.26
Deepglow Skate{4}{U}Creature — FishDoubles counters on anything you've been growing.$0.29
Kruphix's Insight{2}{G}SorceryRefills your hand with enchantments — and you have no hand limit.~$1
Finale of Devastation{X}{G}{G}SorceryThe guaranteed payoff: tutor any creature straight to play, and at X=10 the whole board swings +10 with haste. The stockpile finally has a destination.$45.19
Selvala, Heart of the Wilds{1}{G}{G}Legendary Creature — Elf ScoutTaps for mana equal to the biggest power on the board, and pays you cards for big creatures. Bank faster.$5.44
Hullbreaker Horror{5}{U}{U}Creature — KrakenUncounterable flash 7/8 that bounces a spell or permanent every time you cast anything — the fortress that ends the game.$6.26
Uro, Titan of Nature's Wrath{1}{G}{U}Legendary Creature — Elder GiantRamp, draw and lifegain on every cast and escape — the early game this deck was missing.$3.17
Mana Reflection{4}{G}{G}EnchantmentEvery permanent taps for double. Stacks multiplicatively with Nyxbloom for six-times mana.$2.49
Genesis Wave{X}{G}{G}{G}SorceryThe other convergence button: put the top ten-plus permanents straight onto the battlefield.$0.44

How it plays

The most chess-like deck in the matrix. Kruphix is indestructible as long as your devotion holds, so your commander survives everything, and every turn you don't spend mana you are still getting richer. You hold a huge hand behind cheap walls while three opponents fight each other, and at the moment you choose, a tripled mana pool casts four things in one turn and the game ends. Nothing you do before that turn threatens anyone.

Profile-tuned · Deck 6
Claude’s 5th Place

Golgari Chosen Graveyard — Old Stickfingers

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Old Stickfingers{X}{B}{G} Legendary Creature — HorrorWhen it enters, mill until X creature cards are in your graveyard. A 1/1 that grows with every creature in your yard.$0.31

Deck rarity — by stage

Base80%Uncommon
Tuned85%Rarely seen
Maxed87%Rarely seen

Modeled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (3949 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognize.

Precon seed

Any Golgari graveyard shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$35 $102 total
Why this commander

You choose exactly how much of your library goes to the graveyard and exactly which creature you keep. Almost no commander lets you tune the size of your own graveyard on cast.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Living Death{3}{B}{B}SorceryEveryone's creatures swap with their graveyards. After Stickfingers, yours is vastly better.$4.01
Victimize{2}{B}SorcerySacrifice one creature, reanimate two. The exact converter for a hand-stocked graveyard.$1.67
Eternal Witness{1}{G}{G}Creature — Human ShamanBuys the reanimation spell back for a second go.$1.74
Wall of Blossoms{1}{G}Creature — Plant WallDefense while you set up.$0.26
Putrefy{1}{B}{G}InstantKills a creature or artifact, no regeneration — the clean early answer to a growing threat.$0.32
Mikaeus, the Unhallowed{3}{B}{B}{B}Legendary Creature — Zombie ClericYour whole non-Human board gets undying and +1/+1 — after Living Death, everything has to be killed twice.$25.45
Deadbridge Chant{4}{B}{G}EnchantmentFree value every upkeep from your own stocked yard — the Sheoldred job with zero edicts and zero salt.$0.35
Reanimate{B}SorceryOne mana: the best creature in any graveyard, immediately.$9.08
Hermit Druid{1}{G}Creature — Human DruidOne activation a turn keeps the yard growing without recasting the commander.$8.49
Underrealm Lich{3}{B}{G}Creature — Zombie Elf ShamanEvery draw digs three deep and banks two in the yard — selection and fuel at once.$7.37
Life from the Loam{1}{G}SorceryDredge instead of drawing: lands back to hand, more creatures into the yard.$5.53
Meren of Clan Nel Toth{2}{B}{G}Legendary Creature — Human ShamanFree reanimation every end step as experience accumulates.$1.23
Grave Titan{4}{B}{B}Creature — GiantSix power over three bodies — the reanimation target that rebuilds a board alone.$0.79

How it plays

The single most convergent deck in the matrix, and unusually it removes the luck from convergence. Most graveyard decks hope the right cards get milled; Stickfingers lets you pay X and deliberately stock exactly as many creatures as you want. You spend the game looking like you are doing nothing — a small frog-thing and a pile of dead cards — and then one Living Death turns twenty turns of quiet setup into a full board in a single cast.

  • Rate: a scalable one-card graveyard filler for two mana plus X.
  • Friendly: mostly clean — you fill your own yard. with Sheoldred swapped for Deadbridge Chant, nothing here touches another player's board at all.

That total is the 13 upgrades listed above, plus about 18 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$260), plus the 3 Game Changers below (~$69). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Bracket 2
Core2.73Bracket 3
Upgraded
On the 2/3 line · 0 of 3 Game Changers used

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modeled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
The Maxed rung — 3 color-legal Game Changers, about $69
Game Changer$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Crop Rotation$4Takes the ramp slot held by Sylvan Caryatid. Search your library for a land card, put that card onto the battlefield, then shuffle.
Orcish Bowmasters$47Takes the removal slot held by Tragic Slip. When this creature enters and whenever an opponent draws a card except the first one they draw in each of their draw steps, this creature deals 1 damage to any target.
Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lantern$19Takes the finisher slot held by Morbid Opportunist. Whenever an opponent sacrifices a nontoken permanent or discards a permanent card, you may put that card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under your control.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are not a shortlist — they are the cards the Maxed hundred runs. Each was tried in several slots in the list it would join, kept only where the deck did not measurably get worse over 3,000 simulated games, and confirmed afterwards on a seed the selection never saw. Prices are Scryfall market values.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: The most graveyard-hate-exposed deck in the matrix, and that is reflected in its Assembly score. A single Rest in Peace is close to a concession. Note it is also the cheapest build sitting in the Capstone row — a budget path into the slot, not a capstone.
Claude’s 5th Place

Fifth, now clean: Sheoldred's edicts are swapped for Deadbridge Chant, restoring Friendly to 5 while Mikaeus keeps the yard genuinely scary. The remaining knock is the one no card swap can touch — this is still the most graveyard-hate-exposed build in the matrix, and one Rest in Peace is close to a concession.

Profile-tuned · Deck 6
Claude’s Choice

Sultai ETB Doubling — Yarok

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Yarok, the Desecrated{2}{B}{G}{U} Legendary Creature — Elemental HorrorDeathtouch, lifelink. If a permanent entering the battlefield causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, it triggers an additional time.$0.40

Deck rarity — by stage

Base56%Fairly familiar
Tuned66%Fairly familiar
Maxed71%Uncommon

Modeled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (2489 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognize.

Precon seed

Faceless Menace Commander 2019 OOP — hunt it ~$50 $141 total
Why this commander

Doubles every enters-the-battlefield trigger you have while he is on the battlefield — and as your commander, he is never more than one recast away. Every value creature in the deck becomes twice the card without changing a thing.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Panharmonicon{4}ArtifactStacks with Yarok: three triggers per ETB. The convergence multiplier.$7.01
Wavesifter{3}{G}{U}Creature — ElementalEvoke {G}{U}: two mana for four Clues with Yarok out — draw that also feeds Eternal Witness.$0.28
Acidic Slime{3}{G}{G}Creature — OozeDestroy two permanents instead of one — answers the dangerous thing early.$0.35
Mulldrifter{4}{U}Creature — ElementalFour cards for five mana with Yarok out.$0.45
Eternal Witness{1}{G}{G}Creature — Human ShamanReturns two cards from the graveyard.$1.74
Sepulchral Primordial{5}{B}{B}Creature — AvatarTakes two creatures from opponents' graveyards instead of one.$0.40
Craterhoof Behemoth{5}{G}{G}{G}Creature — BeastYarok doubles the trigger: the team gets +2X/+2X and trample, twice over. The cleanest kill in the row.$23.77
Thassa, Deep-Dwelling{3}{U}Legendary Enchantment Creature — GodBlinks your best ETB creature every end step, for free, forever — an indestructible engine wipes cannot touch.$25.95
Deadeye Navigator{4}{U}{U}Creature — SpiritSoulbond: two mana re-buys any ETB on demand, at instant speed.$3.02
Uro, Titan of Nature's Wrath{1}{G}{U}Legendary Creature — Elder GiantDraw, land and 6 life per cast with Yarok. The early game and the late game in one card.$3.17
Wonder{3}{U}Creature — IncarnationFrom the graveyard, your whole board flies. A win condition that costs no mana.$2.92
Risen Reef{1}{G}{U}Creature — ElementalEvery Elemental (Yarok included) draws into more board — doubled.$0.31
Zagoth Triome-LandAll three colors, fetchable — the honest mana upgrade a three-color deck actually feels.$21.98

How it plays

The most elegant capstone. Yarok reads as a modest rules change and quietly doubles the entire deck — every value creature you already wanted to play becomes twice the card. Deathtouch and lifelink on a 3/5 body means the aggressive decks leave you alone while it happens. Where Muldrotha grinds by replaying things, Yarok compounds by making each play worth double, which is a cleaner and much less hate-vulnerable version of the same 'more resources than the table' plan.

Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lantern$19Takes the finisher slot held by Craterhoof Behemoth. Whenever an opponent sacrifices a nontoken permanent or discards a permanent card, you may put that card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under your control.

variants.detailHtml:
Base Variant · Deck 6
Claude’s 3rd Place

The Endless Harvest — Muldrotha

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Muldrotha, the Gravetide{3}{B}{G}{U} Legendary Creature — Elemental AvatarEach turn, play a land plus one artifact, creature, enchantment and planeswalker from your graveyard.$1.99

Deck rarity — by stage

Base66%Fairly familiar
Tuned71%Uncommon
Maxed75%Uncommon

Modeled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (1097 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognize.

Precon seed

Faceless Menace Commander 2019 OOP — hunt it ~$50 $160 total
Why this commander

One permanent of every type per turn, out of your own graveyard, for free. It turns the graveyard into a second hand and makes removal aimed at you close to worthless.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Sidisi, Undead Vizier{3}{B}{B}Creature — Naga ShamanETB tutor for any card. Toolbox access.$8.13
The Scarab God{3}{U}{B}Legendary Creature — GodA second reanimation track running every end step.$5.25
Grave Titan{4}{B}{B}Creature — GiantSix power across three bodies, and it rebuilds you.$0.79
Living Death{3}{B}{B}SorceryA wipe you profit from — the convergence turn.$4.01
Kokusho, the Evening Star{4}{B}{B}Legendary Creature — Dragon SpiritRestored under the full brief: dies, drains 15 across the table — and this deck replays it.$26.21
Heroic Intervention{1}{G}InstantRestored under the full brief: hexproof and indestructible for the team — the wipe answer.$15.59

How it plays

Fill the yard on purpose, land Muldrotha, then play two or three extra cards a turn forever. The most decision-dense deck of the six.

Ratings

Engine rating — community value axes

Card Adv.
Clock
Interaction
Resilience
Assembly66%
  • Longevity: excellent.
  • Fortress: the gap — it does very little before turn five or six.

What Keith said

Seems good, playing out of graveyard will be fun.
Endorsed as-is — nothing changed
  • Nothing changed, on purpose. Keith had no criticism of this one, so inventing a swap to justify the label would be dishonest. This is the build exactly as it stood, carrying his sign-off.
  • What he is endorsing is the thing this deck does that no other deck in the lineup does: four independent recursion engines running at once, so removal aimed at you mostly does not matter.
  • One addition under the full $165 Capstone brief. Kokusho, the Evening Star ($26.21) and Heroic Intervention ($15.59) — the two cards the earlier sub-$10 pricing rule stripped out — are restored. Kokusho is a 15-life swing across the table that Muldrotha and The Scarab God can replay; Heroic Intervention is the answer to the board wipe this deck otherwise just absorbs. $118.18 to $159.98.
  • The one caution still stands. A single Rest in Peace or Leyline of the Void turns eight of these cards off. If someone at the table runs graveyard hate, this is the deck that feels it.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

Headroom35 cards
Upgrade value~$17 ea

The two dot rows score 35 cards costing about $601 in total — roughly $17 a card, or 5.8 upgrades per $100. That total is the 6 upgrades listed above, plus about 26 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$450), plus the 3 Game Changers below (~$94). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

The next cards you would buy
  • Life from the Loam
  • Ramunap Excavator
  • Crucible of Worlds
  • World Shaper
  • Perpetual Timepiece

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Bracket 2
Core2.77Bracket 3
Upgraded
On the 2/3 line · 0 of 3 Game Changers used

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modeled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
The Maxed rung — 3 color-legal Game Changers, about $94
Game Changer$What it replaces, and what it buys you
Crop Rotation$4Takes the ramp slot held by Arcane Signet. Search your library for a land card, put that card onto the battlefield, then shuffle.
Demonic Tutor$62Takes the tutor slot held by Sidisi, Undead Vizier. Search your library for a card, put that card into your hand, then shuffle.
Worldly Tutor$28Takes the tutor slot held by Corpse Connoisseur. Search your library for a creature card, reveal it, then shuffle and put the card on top.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are not a shortlist — they are the cards the Maxed hundred runs. Each was tried in several slots in the list it would join, kept only where the deck did not measurably get worse over 3,000 simulated games, and confirmed afterwards on a seed the selection never saw. Prices are Scryfall market values.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Strong as built. Its two real risks are graveyard hate and dying before turn six.
Claude’s 3rd Place

Third, upgraded: Kokusho and Heroic Intervention — the two cards the sub-$10 rule stripped — are restored under the full $165 brief, taking it to $160. Four recursion engines and 5/5 Longevity stand. It stays third because eight cards still fold to one Rest in Peace and it does little before turn five; the gap to the two above is now smaller than it was.
